name: Homegrown Plate
tagline: Grow it. Cook it. Keep it.

audience.main: UK beginners growing their own food, from a windowsill or balcony up to a small garden or allotment
audience.also: Intermediate UK home growers who want to waste less of what they grow

voice.how_it_sounds: First person, like Mark talking over the fence: a small garden with four raised beds and a greenhouse, a dad who grew up watching his own dad on the allotment, two young sons. Plain English, short sentences, no jargon. Honest about what goes wrong. Cares most about not wasting what you grow.
do: Use plain words for gardening jobs (sow, plant out, pick, store)
Mention real UK conditions: frost, wet autumns, small gardens, greenhouses, windowsills
Lean on the whole journey: sow it, grow it, cook it, keep it
voice.never_words_source: Usual AI words plus US gardening words, Mark 5-6 Nov 2026
voice.jargon_to_avoid: Mark wants plain terms, not complex gardening jargon
voice.glut_wording: Vary it: 'too many' for things you count (Brussels sprouts, courgettes, apples), 'too much' for leaves and the rest, also 'more than you can eat', 'a bumper crop', 'all those'. Use the word 'glut' rarely. Never for herbs. Mark, 6 Nov 2026.

never_post: Anything not backed by the site

commission.note: No links earn commission yet (affiliate disclosure page says the site may in future). Add any affiliate domain here and every post linking to it must start with 'Ad'.

channels.tiktok_note: Mark has no TikTok account yet (6 Nov 2026). TikTok captions are still made so the daily TikTok task can start the day the account exists.
channels.accounts_source: Mark, 6 Nov 2026 (Instagram, Facebook Page and Pinterest already exist)

ai_images: Never generated. Only Mark's photos and videos and the site's own images are used.

niche_crops.rule: Never featured in reels, carousels, Stories or pins (they still appear in the site's monthly lists). Mark asked to avoid posts about niche crops, 6 Nov 2026; list drafted by Claude for Mark to edit.
